answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The beacon multiplier is published, charged in wharf, and lantern lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 872 identities would post 1957 proofs and burn roughly 10 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
